question: Can the frozen Lead Quality and Inventory Availability components be integrated into one Lead Opportunity Score with a governed fallback policy that improves prioritization of serviceable conversion opportunities?
hypothesis: A multiplicative Lead Opportunity Score and bounded top-3 fallback policy will increase the concentration of serviceable scheduled-visit opportunities at the frozen P85 capacity, while exposing the tradeoff against conversion-only ranking.
primary_change: integrate Lead Quality and Inventory Availability end-to-end and freeze the fallback recommendation policy
secondary_changes: define joint_success as scheduled_visit_30d AND confirmed_serviceable
freeze K=3 using folds 1-3 and report fold 4 as the final confirmation

scoring_time.timestamp_definition: same T1/T2 score_time used by Modelo 3; T0 retains no high-priority routing gate

target.joint_operational_proxy: scheduled_visit_30d AND confirmed_serviceable at score time
target.confirmed_serviceable: current requested spot is available as-of OR at least one final top-3 fallback recommendation is available as-of

population.fallback_trigger: current requested spot not confirmed available as-of

validation.fallback_k_selection: K chosen from folds 1-3; fold 4 used as final confirmation
validation.combined_score: metrics computed independently inside each fold and stage; raw scores are never rank-mixed across folds

decision_rule.fallback: prefer K=3 if design folds materially improve complete-list coverage versus K=5 while preserving bounded business constraints
decision_rule.combined: promote the combined score if it consistently improves the joint operational proxy; conversion-only degradation must be retained as a guardrail rather than hidden

items.evidence: OOF temporal prediction from E007 trajectory CV
uses lead/request data and point-in-time inventory only
used only through the existing 30-day conversion proxy
